title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This document centralizes Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is the canonical reference for employees, contractors, and approved vendors.

Scope

Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and vendors that interact with Redwood systems, data, or procure goods and services on behalf of the company. Teams may implement stricter controls where required; the stricter control takes precedence.

Roles and responsibilities

- People Ops: policy owner for travel, internal templates, and company-wide communication.
- Finance & Legal: owners for procurement approvals, expense policy, contracting, and vendor legal reviews.
- Security: owner for access control standards, data classification, vendor security assessments, and audit logging.
- Engineering Managers / Team Leads: approve role-based access requests and sign off on changes that directly affect their services.
- IT / Platform: provisioning and deprovisioning, quarterly access reviews, and IAM tooling operations.

1) Access and permissions

Purpose: Enforce least privilege, consistent role definitions, and an auditable request/approval workflow.

Key controls:
- Identity provider: Okta (primary). All employee SSO accounts are provisioned through Okta.
- Role-based groups: use predefined groups (e.g., eng-readonly, eng-pager, infra-admin). Custom roles require Manager + Security approval.
- Least privilege provisioning: new hires receive baseline roles; additional access requested via the Access Portal with justification and duration.
- Access request flow:
  1. Submit request via Access Portal (https://access.redwood.internal) with justification and requested duration.
  2. Manager approval required for non-baseline roles.
  3. Security review required for production, customer data, or RESTRICTED system access.
- Emergency "break-glass":
  - To request emergency elevated access, email oncall-security@redwood.com with reason and pager evidence. IT will provision a time-limited token and log the session.
  - A Change Record and Security Event entry must be filed within 48 hours after emergency access is used.
- Access certification: automated quarterly certification is run; owners must re-assert approvals within 7 days or access will be revoked.

2) Change management

Purpose: Minimize production risk while enabling timely operational and product changes.

Change categories:
- Standard change: pre-approved, low-risk (e.g., small config flips). No CAB required; follow canary rollout and logging requirements.
- Normal change: requires RFC in the Change Registry and CAB approval prior to scheduling (examples: schema migrations, infra changes).
- Emergency change: applied to mitigate active outages; retroactive RFC and CAB review required within 48 hours.

Normal change process:
1. Create RFC in Change Registry (/confluence/policies-and-process/change-management/rfcs) including owner, rollback plan, test plan, impact analysis, and runbook links.
2. Impacted service owners and Security review within 48 hours.
3. Book CAB slot (weekly CAB: Wednesday 10:00–11:00 PT). CAB includes Eng Platform, SRE, Security, and Product as needed.
4. If approved, schedule within designated maintenance windows and notify stakeholders 48 hours prior.
5. Execute with a runbook, run post-change verification tests, and update monitoring dashboards.
6. Close RFC and publish change record. If production impact exceeds 1 minute of user-visible outage, file a postmortem.

Maintenance windows:
- Preferred window: Saturday 02:00–06:00 PT for infra and low-traffic changes.
- Major migrations: require freeze period communicated at least 7 days in advance.

3) Data management

Purpose: Protect customer and company data through clear classification, handling, and retention controls.

Classification levels:
- PUBLIC: content intended for public distribution (marketing, blog posts).
- INTERNAL: non-sensitive internal information (team wiki, playbooks).
- CONFIDENTIAL: business-sensitive material (roadmaps, non-public contracts).
- RESTRICTED: customer data, keys, credentials, and regulated data (PII/PHI).

Handling rules:
- RESTRICTED: encrypted at rest and in transit; access limited to approved roles and audited.
- CONFIDENTIAL: may be shared under NDA with Legal approval.
- INTERNAL: internal-only; do not post to public repos or external services without review.

Retention summary (owners listed):
- System logs: 90 days hot, 2 years cold — Security & SRE owner.
- Audit trails & access logs: 7 years — Security & Compliance owner.
- Customer PII: per contract; default 3 years after contract termination unless otherwise required.
- Source code: retained indefinitely in repositories with branch protection and backups.

Data deletion and eDiscovery:
- Route deletion or eDiscovery requests to security-legal@redwood.com. Legal SLA: acknowledge within 72 hours; target full response within 30 days where feasible.

Encryption and keys:
- Private deployments: customer-managed KMS/HSM.
- Hosted: Redwood-managed KMS with strict access controls; key access limited to Security and Platform engineers on a need-to-know basis.

4) Procurement and expenses

Purpose: Ensure consistent purchasing, financial controls, and budget stewardship.

Approval thresholds (summary):
- <$1,000: Manager approval.
- $1,000–$50,000: Manager + Finance approval.
- > $50,000: Manager + Finance + Procurement Committee and Legal contract review.

Procurement flow:
1. Submit purchase request in Procurement Portal (procure.redwood.internal) with justification, cost center, and vendor details.
2. Finance reviews budget and pricing alternatives.
3. For SaaS or integrations, Security reviews vendor data flows and integration risk.
4. Procurement issues PO and coordinates signature routing.

Expense policy (employees):
- Use corporate booking tool (Concur) where possible. Pre-approval required for exceptions.
- Submit receipts within 30 days. Per diem applies per the company travel table.
- Non-reimbursable: personal entertainment, upgrades without approval, missing receipts > $25.
- Corporate card holders: reconcile monthly with receipts attached.

5) Vendor management

Purpose: Reduce vendor and supply-chain risk and ensure contractual and security safeguards.

Onboarding checklist:
- Complete vendor intake form (procure.redwood.internal/vendor-intake).
- Security questionnaire (SIG-lite) for vendors; full security review for vendors accessing company or customer data.
- Legal: DPA required for data processing; indemnity and limitation clauses reviewed.
- Procurement & Finance: sanctions and financial viability checks.
- Operational: assign vendor owner, define SLAs, escalation contacts, and onboarding timeline.

Periodic reviews:
- Quarterly health checks for strategic vendors.
- Annual security reassessment for vendors with production access or those storing RESTRICTED data.

Offboarding checklist:
- Revoke vendor access (Okta groups, API keys) and confirm asset return.
- Validate data deletion per contract and retain proof in the Vendor File.

6) Travel policies

Purpose: Provide safe, cost-effective business travel and reduce administrative friction.

Pre-approval and booking:
- All travel requires manager pre-approval via Travel Portal. International travel requires People Ops notification; high-risk countries require Security clearance.
- Preferred booking: Concur or corporate travel agency. Exceptions need written pre-approval.

Allowed expenses:
- Flights: economy for <8 hours; business class >8 hours with Director approval.
- Hotels: standard business hotels; follow per diem in high-cost regions.
- Meals: itemized receipts required; per diem applies where used.

Safety and insurance:
- Company travel insurance covers business travel. International travelers should register with People Ops prior to departure.
- Emergency contacts: travel-emergency@redwood.com and People Ops oncall.

7) Internal templates and forms

Canonical templates (Confluence):
- PRD template: /confluence/product-docs/design-specs/prd-template.
- RFC / Change request: /confluence/policies-and-process/change-management/rfc-template.
- Vendor intake: /confluence/finance-and-legal/vendor-intake-template.
- Expense reimbursement: /confluence/finance-and-legal/expense-claim-template.
- Travel request: /confluence/policies-and-process/travel/travel-request-template.

Templates include guidance notes and example completions for common scenarios.

Audit, compliance, and review cadence

- Policy review: Annual review owned by People Ops with input from Finance, Security, and Engineering.
- Internal audits: Security and Finance conduct scheduled audits and publish findings and remediation plans.
- Exceptions: Must be documented and approved by policy owner and Legal where applicable.

Contacts and escalation matrix

- Security: security@redwood.com (incidents, access, security questionnaires).
- Procurement & Finance: procurement@redwood.com, finance@redwood.com.
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com (travel, templates, policy questions).
- IT / Platform: it-ops@redwood.com.

Appendix A — Example RFC checklist

- Title and owner.
- Services impacted and stakeholder list.
- Rollout plan with canary percentages and metrics to monitor.
- Rollback plan with step-by-step commands or runbook link.
- Test plan and staging validation criteria.
- Scheduled window and expected downtime.

Appendix B — Quick reference

Approval thresholds:
- <$1,000: manager.
- $1,000–$50,000: manager + finance.
- > $50,000: procurement committee + legal.

Data classification quick guide:
- PUBLIC: OK to publish.
- INTERNAL: internal use only.
- CONFIDENTIAL: limited distribution.
- RESTRICTED: encryption and strict controls required.

Change windows:
- Regular maintenance: Saturday 02:00–06:00 PT.
- Emergency changes: follow emergency change process and document post-event.

Change log

- 2024-06-15: Initial consolidated policy published (Maya Chen).
- 2025-10-01: Added procurement thresholds and vendor security questionnaire (Reviewed: Alejandro Ruiz).
- 2026-03-04: Minor edits to change management windows and travel guidance (Updated by Maya Chen).
- 2026-03-25: Published consolidated update including vendor onboarding checklist and access certification details (Maya Chen).

Notes

This is a living document. Teams should submit RFCs for policy changes via the Change Registry. For team-level process templates, follow the linked templates above.
